results.answer:
Southwest's 87 737 MAX 8 aircraft were all operating with MCAS v1.7.3 as of January 1, 2024, and FAA AD 2024-01-02 requires installation of MCAS v2.0 or later by May 15, 2024. Southwest's fleet-wide status lists AD 2024-01-02 as "COMPLIANCE DUE," with software updates scheduled February-May 2024 in phases of roughly 10 aircraft per month, targeting MCAS v2.0 via Boeing SB Rev 2. The G-ABCD report identifies the current version as MCAS v1.7.3 against a required v2.0, flags the status as non-compliant with the deadline not yet reached, and notes the aircraft remains airworthy under v1.7.3 until the deadline, with a maintenance slot scheduled April 22-23, 2024.

Southwest's earlier MCAS-related ADs are recorded as compliant: AD 2020-05-11 (pre-service compliance November 2020) and AD 2022-03-07 (completed April 2022), both for all 87 aircraft. MCAS v1.7.2 was released May 2020 and required by FAA AD 2020-05-11. Under 14 CFR Part 39, operators of 737-8 and 737-9 aircraft are legally required to comply with all applicable ADs, and non-compliance renders the aircraft unairworthy for operation under FAA jurisdiction.
